name: Northwestern Game Jam
oneLiner: Four stories in five weeks, and one question throughout: who has more claim to a home?

context.partner: Northwestern Game Jam 2026 · theme “Twist of Fate”
context.role: Pitched the starting concept; design documents and in-game writing; built in Unity

blocks.title: A ghost story about who owns a house
blocks.text:
Northwestern Game Jam 2026 gave teams five weeks, the theme Twist of Fate and a showcase on May 9. The four of us ended up with **Candell Handles**. A college student with a side hustle in Daoist rituals gets a call from a developer: a staged, move-in-ready house keeps scaring buyers away, and they will pay $5,000 to make it stop by Friday night.

The ghost is the last resident, who refused to sell and died there. The twist belongs to the exorcist: she thinks she was hired to solve a problem, and she is the last step of it.

media.caption: Title screen: Candell’s dorm desk, the talismans buried under pizza and soda cans.

blocks.title: Rules borrowed from Parasite and Papers, Please
blocks.text:
Our references were films and games. **Parasite** gave every version its question: the people living inside a house may have more claim to it than the person on the paperwork. **Papers, Please** gave the Airbnb version its verb: read a booking request, approve or deny it, live with the money. In the realtor version, house hunters were to chatter like the radio in Two Point Hospital, chipper and deadpan.

The final game invents its own bad reference: @spiritkween404, an influencer whose exorcism guide admits, “i have not personally tested this but the theory is solid.”

blocks.title: Twenty pitches, one roommate in the walls
blocks.text:
We each pitched five ideas, twenty in all, and ranked our favourites. My **Roommate** pitch made all four lists: your perfect new roommate has been living inside your walls since before you posted the listing. It fit the theme without forcing, because the lucky coincidence was engineered.

The design gave the player a mundane reason to touch everything, rearranging furniture by day, and took their voice away by night: dialogue options grey out chapter by chapter, still readable, no longer clickable. I set up the first prototype in Godot 4, one clickable living room.

blocks.title: Four stories, one question
blocks.text:
Between April 7 and May 4 the story changed three times. The question stayed; what you do changed.
! Version | In the docs | You play | You
Roommate | Apr 7–9 | a student subletting for the summer | rearrange furniture, lose your lines
Airbnb | Apr 9–16 | a student who inherits a house | vet booking requests, read documents
Magnolia Heights | Apr 17–30 | a new realtor on a haunted block | hide the haunting from buyers
Candell Handles | May 4–9 | a student exorcist | collect, hide, decide how she leaves
Some turns were scope. My note in the Airbnb bible: we couldn’t build a live house interior, so the laptop had to be the whole game.

blocks.title: The question that survived every pivot
blocks.text: Who is the real parasite — the person profiting off a dead woman’s home, or the people who actually lived there?

blocks.title: Reuse the template, cut the rest
blocks.text:
The final game runs in Unity on a first-person horror template. The system doc’s first rule: reuse its inventory, lockpicking, hint prompts and readable papers instead of rebuilding them. On May 5 a deadline build list cut the rest. Cutscenes became black screens with subtitles (AI video later put the opening and ending back), Candell became a first-person camera with no model to rig, three seals became one.

The story lives on paper: a newspaper, an obituary, a developer’s final notice, seven letters. I checked in 18 changes between May 7 and showcase morning.

media.caption: The house at night in the Unity editor; the camera preview shows the marble maze on the couch.

blocks.title: Two endings, decided by your hands
blocks.text:
You pick the lock, the grandmother appears, and a ghost cat leads you through the house: a flashlight, the letters, a marble maze on the couch, a basement chest whose code is the date on her last letter. Then she starts hunting you.

Two paths stay open. Collect pies for a pistol with one bullet and erase her for good, or find five charms and send her on with a ritual at the pool. The ending follows what you do, not what you carry.

media.caption: Opening cutscene: Candell at her desk, minutes before the developer calls.

blocks.title: The plan said polish; the story moved
blocks.text: On paper, our concept locked on April 10 and the last week was polish only, “no new mechanics, no new content.” In the files, the final story is dated May 4, five days before the showcase, and its system doc still lists open decisions.
